issues.description: The problem statement, template code, REST resource and tests expect a PersonService method named addParent(Person person, Person parent). However, the solution's PersonService implements a method named registerParent(Person person, Person parent) instead of addParent. This name mismatch is structural: PersonResource and unit/integration tests call addParent, but the solution class does not provide that method, which would prevent the code from compiling and confuses students about the required API.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the service API consistent: rename the solution method registerParent(...) to addParent(...), or add a public addParent(Person person, Person parent) method that delegates to registerParent(...). Ensure method name and signature match the template, problem statement and tests so PersonResource and the tests compile and the intended API is clear to students.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect a PersonService method named addParent(Person person, Person parent). In the solution implementation the corresponding method is named registerParent(Person person, Person parent). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (adding/registering a parent for a person) creates a mapping confusion: students reading the problem and template will implement or call addParent, while the solution exposes registerParent. Tests and PersonResource expect addParent, so the different name in the solution is likely an unintended inconsistency and increases cognitive load.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method registerParent(...) to addParent(...) so it matches the problem statement and template (or add an addParent(...) wrapper delegating to registerParent(...)). Ensure PersonResource and tests consistently call addParent.
